title: Agents, codebases, and teams — Aditya Khandelwal, Amazon AGI Lab
talk_summary: A team lead at Amazon AGI Lab describes how to make coding agents work across a 10-person team rather than per-IC: shared harness engineering, progressive disclosure, one high-value end-to-end skill, and closing the loop with CI/review/gardening. The core message is that agent effectiveness is a leadership/org problem requiring continuous iteration on a shared setup, not individual prompt tweaks.

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the agent's entry file (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) as a thin index pointing to the right files, cap skill files at ~100 lines, and embed runbook/docs in code comments so the agent finds context only when it reaches that code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's a thin index that can point through the right files and that's what the agent gets in its like first prompt
takeaways.numbers: skill.md hard limit ~100 lines; baseline ~20-25K tokens on first prompt, 40-50K signals a problem

takeaways.what_they_do: Invest in a single skill that takes work from code-done to PR-ready-for-review: opens PR, writes description, handles review comments, fixes CI failures in a loop, running for over an hour unattended.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the moment you're done with your code, it takes care of everything from code done to PR ready for review
takeaways.numbers: skill often ran over an hour

takeaways.technique: Close the loop with automated gardener + CI/review wiring
takeaways.what_they_do: Wire issues/boards into the repo, add CI/CD and automated reviews, and run a nightly 'code gardener' agent that scans the codebase for organizational/structural problems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have like a code gardener that actually goes back and looks through a whole bunch of like every night it'll run

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents not wired correctly flooded the repo with 400-500 issues in weeks; they had to constrain issue creation and route feedback into improving the shared skill instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we blew up to like 4 or 500 issues uh without like, you know, just I think within like a couple of weeks

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat experimental agent-generated code as its own category that opts out of the rigorous standards applied to shippable code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Get it to opt out of all the rigorous other standards you've got across your code base

takeaways.technique: Measure first-prompt context burn as a health metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Judge harness quality by watching what the agent does on the first prompt: does it know where to go, and how many tokens does it burn before real work starts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how much context is it burning when it like immediately? So is it like I think like 20, 25K tokens get taken anyway
